CVE-2024-36401.title: Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in evaluating property name expressions in Geoserver
CVE-2024-36401.description:
GeoServer is an open source server that allows users to share and edit geospatial data. Prior to versions 2.22.6, 2.23.6, 2.24.4, and 2.25.2, multiple OGC request parameters allow Remote Code Execution (RCE) by unauthenticated users through specially crafted input against a default GeoServer installation due to unsafely evaluating property names as XPath expressions.

The GeoTools library API that GeoServer calls evaluates property/attribute names for feature types in a way that unsafely passes them to the commons-jxpath library which can execute arbitrary code when evaluating XPath expressions. This XPath evaluation is intended to be used only by complex feature types (i.e., Application Schema data stores) but is incorrectly being applied to simple feature types as well which makes this vulnerability apply to **ALL** GeoServer instances. CVE-2026-119351.title: Next.js: Cache leak across root param values in nested 'use cache' functions via delayed inner stream metadata
CVE-2026-119351.description: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.2.0 until 16.4.5, Next.js applications with Cache Components enabled can reuse an outer 'use cache' entry across root param values when a nested 'use cache' call reads a root param through next/root-params and returns a value containing pending promises. React Flight can deliver the ready portion to the outer function before the inner cache finishes publishing its root-param dependencies. The outer entry can then complete and be persisted under a key that omits the root param, causing the first written value to be served for other root param values and allowing the outer entry to ignore nested cache tag invalidation and lifetimes. The leaked value is not attacker controlled and depends on which invocation writes the entry first. This variant does not require an existing inner cache entry or a slow cache handler and is not covered by the fix for CVE-2026-103004. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

CVE-2026-99699.title: mm/cma: accept memory of multi-range CMA areas
CVE-2026-99699.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/cma: accept memory of multi-range CMA areas

Patch series "mm/cma: accept memory of CMA areas reserved with
memblock_reserve()", v1.

Pages of allocated CMA areas are released to the buddy allocator with
__free_pages(), which does not check for unaccepted memory.

This usually works because memblock accepts the memory it allocates.

However, multi-range CMA areas, used by hugetlb_cma, and fixed CMA areas
requested with cma=<size>@<base> are reserved with memblock_reserve() and
their memory is never accepted.

On TDX and SEV-SNP guests the first access to such a page is fatal.

To ease the backporting, each case is addressed by a separate patch:
- patch 1 accepts the memory of multi-range CMA areas
- patch 2 does the same for the fixed CMA areas

The second patch won't apply cleanly to 6.6 and 6.12, but I believe the
stable team LLMs will take care of that :)

CVE-2026-99758.title: sctp: account for chunk padding in sctp_init_cause()
CVE-2026-99758.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sctp: account for chunk padding in sctp_init_cause()

sctp_init_cause() accepts a chunk when skb_tailroom() can hold the
cause header and the payload. sctp_addto_chunk() then writes 0-3
bytes of padding before that header so the chunk stays 4-byte
aligned. The check does not include the padding, and the following
skb_put() calls skb_over_panic() from softirq.

Count the padding sctp_addto_chunk() is about to write. The cause
length on the wire stays the header plus the payload.

Found by LLM inspection, triggered and tested the fix.
